title: Operadic algebroids and their complete objects
statement: Use [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-set] for the underlying simplicial-set convention. Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$; small means $\mathcal U$-small and all categories under discussion fit in $\mathcal U'$. For $n\geq2$ and $0<i<n$, the inner horn $\Lambda_i^n\subset\Delta^n$ is the union of all faces except the $i$-th face; $\Delta^n$ is the nerve of the ordered set $[n]$. An infinity category is modeled by a simplicial set in which every map from such an inner horn extends to $\Delta^n$. Spaces are infinity groupoids. A monoidal infinity category $\mathcal V$ is encoded by a cocartesian fibration $\mathcal V^\otimes\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ with Segal fibers $\mathcal V^n$ and operations given by tensor product; inert maps select consecutive subintervals. For a small space $X$, let $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ be the left fibration classified by $[n]\mapsto X^{n+1}$. A $\mathcal V$-algebroid with object space $X$ is a functor $\Delta_X^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal V^\otimes$ over $\Delta^{\mathrm{op}}$ carrying inert maps to cocartesian maps. Its values over $[1]$ are written $A(x,y)$. A morphism over $f:X\to Y$ is a morphism of these algebras from $A$ to $f^*B$. Write $\operatorname{Algd}(\mathcal V)$ for the resulting total infinity category. For a finite set $\{0,\ldots,n\}$, $E^n$ has all mapping objects the tensor unit and all compositions its canonical multiplication. An algebroid $A$ is complete when the map $\operatorname{Map}(E^0,A)\to\operatorname{Map}(E^1,A)$ induced by collapsing $E^1$ to $E^0$ is an equivalence. Write $\operatorname{Cat}_{\mathcal V}$ for the full subcategory of complete algebroids. Fully faithful means equivalence on every mapping object; essentially surjective means surjective on equivalence classes of objects in the underlying category with mapping spaces $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal V}(\mathbf1,A(x,y))$. A presentable infinity category is an accessible infinity category with all small colimits: for some regular cardinal it is generated under that cardinal's filtered colimits by a small collection of objects whose mapping-space functors preserve those colimits. Presentably monoidal means presentable with tensor preserving small colimits separately.
